Reason: The step plans to compute the expected number of incorrect papers by using the average p-value (0.04) as the proportion of false positives, conflating p-values with Type I error/false discovery rates. The nominal Type I error is set by the alpha threshold (typically 0.05), not by the observed average p-value, and the number of incorrect claims cannot be inferred from an average p-value without assumptions about the prevalence of true effects and study power. This could lead to an incorrect solution.
